topic: retrieval-augmented generation for clinical question answering

documents.title: Ward-Round Notes on Citation-Grounded RAG for Clinical Question Answering
documents.summary: Internal reading notes comparing citation-grounded retrieval-augmented generation pipelines for bedside clinical question answering; recommends passage-level citations and abstention when retrieval confidence is low.
documents.passage: Citation-grounded RAG answered 41 of 50 bedside clinical questions with every claim linked to a retrieved guideline passage; the remaining 9 were correctly deferred because no passage cleared the confidence threshold.

documents.title: Hallucination Audit of a Hospital Formulary RAG Assistant
documents.summary: Audit of a retrieval-augmented medical question answering assistant built on a hospital formulary; catalogues unsupported dosing claims and shows that retrieval re-ranking halves them.
documents.passage: Re-ranking retrieved formulary passages before generation reduced unsupported dosing statements from 12.4% to 5.9% of answers in the medical QA audit set.

papers.title: Chart-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Question Answering over Electronic Health Records
papers.abstract: We present a retrieval-augmented generation system that retrieves structured chart segments and free-text notes from electronic health records to answer clinicians' patient-specific questions, improving exact-match accuracy over note-only retrieval.
papers.full_text: Chart-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Question Answering over Electronic Health Records. Abstract: We retrieve structured chart segments alongside free-text notes and condition generation on both. On a held-out set of 1,200 clinician questions, chart-aware retrieval improves exact-match accuracy from 61.3% to 72.8% over note-only retrieval while keeping every answer linked to a retrieved record segment.

papers.title: Guideline Graph Re-Ranking Reduces Hallucination in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
papers.abstract: Re-ranking retrieved passages with a clinical guideline graph before generation cuts unsupported statements in medical question answering, measured on a benchmark of guideline-derived questions.
papers.full_text: Guideline Graph Re-Ranking Reduces Hallucination in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering. Abstract: Passages retrieved for a medical question are re-ranked by their distance to the question's concepts in a clinical guideline graph. Unsupported statements fall from 18.2% to 7.5% of generated sentences on 900 guideline-derived questions.

articles.title: Retrieval-augmented large language models for answering clinicians' drug-dosing questions: a prospective evaluation
articles.abstract: Prospective study of a retrieval-augmented assistant answering 300 drug-dosing questions from ward clinicians.

articles.title: Citation fidelity of retrieval-augmented generation in emergency medicine question answering
articles.abstract: Benchmark of citation fidelity for retrieval-augmented answers to emergency medicine questions.
